prompt_text: I am planning a trip. Should I book on Airbnb, Vrbo, or Booking.com, and how do I find a good host?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer
- There’s no single “best” site — choose by the kind of place you want and how you like to book:
  - Vrbo: best for whole-home rentals (families/groups, cottages, beach houses).
  - Airbnb: biggest variety (unique stays, entire places, private rooms); good for hosts who provide a local touch and for longer/quirky stays.
  - Booking.com: great for hotels and instantly confirmed apartments; good for last-minute bookings and flexible/corporate travel.

Which to pick depends on your trip — tell me destination, dates, group size, and priorities (price, cancellation flexibility, instant booking, family-friendly, pets, hosts who interact), and I’ll recommend one.

How to find a good host — step-by-step checklist
1. Pick the right platform/filter
   - Use Vrbo for whole homes and family-style rentals.
   - Use Airbnb for variety, unique homes, and monthly stays/host interaction.
   - Use Booking.com for hotels/apartments with instant confirmation and simpler cancellation/payment options.
   - Use filters: entire place, number of bedrooms/beds, pet-friendly, self check-in, washer, Wi‑Fi, etc.

2. Evaluate reviews
   - Prioritize listings with many recent reviews (last 6–12 months).
   - Read the latest 10–20 reviews and look for recurring comments (cleanliness, accuracy, noise, host responsiveness).
   - Pay attention to recent negative reviews — a pattern is a red flag.

3. Check the host profile and badges
   - Look for Superhost / top-rated / premier-host or similar badges (indicates consistency).
   - Check response rate/time and how long the host has been active.
   - See if the host has other listings and whether those have good reviews.

4. Verify listing accuracy
   - Compare photos to the description and map. Street View and neighborhood photos help judge location and surroundings.
   - Confirm sleeping arrangements (which beds are in what rooms) and exact number of guests allowed.
   - Check total price (cleaning fee, service fee, extra guest fee, local taxes).

5. Read the house rules & cancellation policy
   - Make sure rules match your plans (no parties, quiet hours, check-in/out times).
   - Choose a cancellation policy that suits you (flexible vs. strict). For risky dates, prefer flexible or moderate.

6. Ask questions before booking (and use the reply to judge the host)
   - Ask about self-check-in, parking, noise, recent renovations, or anything unclear.
   - A good host replies promptly, politely, and with useful details.

7. Look for practical signals of a reliable host
   - Clear check-in instructions and house manual.
   - Recent photos and up-to-date calendar.
   - Willingness to confirm things like early check-in or luggage storage in advance.

8. Safety and fraud prevention
   - Always book and pay through the platform (don’t accept direct-wire/PayPal requests).
   - Avoid listings with extremely low prices or brand-new listings with no reviews unless you can verify the host and photos.
   - Save screenshots of the listing and messages in case of disputes.

Example pre-booking message you can send (copy/paste)
“Hi — we’re [number] guests traveling from [city/country], arriving [date] and departing [date]. We especially need [parking/Wi‑Fi/kitchen/pets]. Could you confirm self check-in, exact sleeping arrangements, and if there are any neighborhood noise issues? Also, do you accept early check-in around [time]? Thanks!”

Red flags to avoid
- Host asks you to pay outside the platform.
- No/very few reviews, or reviews that are all short and generic.
- Frequent last-minute cancellations or many negative comments about cleanliness or accuracy.
- Listing photos look stock/duplicated (reverse-image search if unsure).
- Host won’t answer basic logistical questions.

Platform-specific tips
- Airbnb: Use Superhost and “Instant Book” filters if you want reliable, quick bookings. Check for extra guest fees and cleaning fees.
- Vrbo: Good for properties marketed to families — check rates for high-season weeks and security deposit policies.
- Booking.com: Often shows pay-at-property and free cancellation options; good for hotels and business travel. Read apartment host reviews carefully because Booking aggregates both hotels and private rentals.

If you want, tell me:
- Destination, dates, how many people, and top priorities (budget, flexibility, whole home vs room, pets, etc.)
I’ll suggest the right platform, a shortlist of what to filter for, and even a draft message tailored to your trip.
